title: Boeing 737 MAX: MCAS certification assumptions, pilot-response model failure, and warning/alert overload
summary: The Boeing 737 MAX record is promoted as a warning-governance and assumption-validation case. Rev0006 does not attempt a full accident reconstruction. It preserves official-source claims that design/certification assumptions about pilot response, MCAS behavior, single-sensor vulnerability, multiple alerts, production pressure, and oversight failed under real accident conditions.

status_history.note: Seed/candidate queue listed Boeing 737 MAX MCAS under software/IT and transportation engineering failures.

type_payload.incident_class: commercial aviation design/certification failure with two fatal crashes
type_payload.system: 737 MAX flight-control augmentation, AOA sensors, cockpit alerts, pilot procedures/training, certification and oversight process

sequence_of_events.event: MAX design added MCAS to address handling/feel requirements in part of the flight envelope.
Safety assessments and certification processes relied on assumptions about pilot recognition and response to uncommanded MCAS-related trim.
Real accident scenarios involved erroneous AOA data, unintended MCAS operation, repeated nose-down trim, and multiple flight-deck alerts/indications.
Official reviews found that assumptions, design criteria, certification oversight, and corrective actions needed significant revision.

type_payload.proximate_cause: Not encoded as a single proximate-cause statement in rev0006; official accident-final-report extraction remains pending. This record centers on certified design assumptions and warning/alert handling.
warning_signals: hazard-assessment assumptions about immediate appropriate pilot response
internal/organizational pressure and oversight warnings in official reports
type_payload.proof_burden_observation: The case shows assumptions about ideal human recovery being treated as safety credit; rev0006 records this as an assumption-validation failure rather than a simple operator-error narrative.
contributing_factors: production pressure and oversight failures as described by House report
multiple flight-deck alerts not comprehensively evaluated in safety assessment
certification guidance allowed pilot-response assumptions without sufficient validation tools
latent_conditions: Derivative-aircraft certification and delegation structure require separate future records.
Human factors and cockpit alert complexity were not fully integrated into hazard classification.
decisions_that_mattered: Classifying hazards based on assumed pilot response.
Not simulating all failure modes and combined alerts/indications in the safety assessment.
Not requiring design/procedural/training mitigations robust to inconsistent pilot actions until after the accidents.
type_payload.record_grain_warning: This is a certification-assumption shell. Full crash records require national accident reports and separate victim-sensitive treatment.

handling_notes: 346 people died; keep casualty details necessary but not graphic.
Do not shift blame onto pilots; the record explicitly tracks system design, alerts, assumptions, training, and certification context.
Future records should include Indonesian and Ethiopian official reports before detailed accident narratives.
